title: 35m Taller Than the Eiffel Tower: How India Built the World's Highest Railway Bridge

scenes.voiceoverText: For seventy-five years, heavy winter snow could cut Kashmir off from India's railway network.
scenes.captionMarkup: For *75 years,* heavy winter snow could cut *Kashmir* off from India's *railway network.*

scenes.voiceoverText: So India built the highest railway bridge on Earth right across the Himalayas. Stay with me, because one extreme survival number explains everything.
scenes.beatACaption: So India built the *highest railway bridge* on Earth right across the *Himalayas.*
scenes.beatBCaption: Stay with me — *one extreme number* in this video explains *everything.*

scenes.voiceoverText: Between Bakkal and Kauri in Jammu and Kashmir lies a sheer canyon above the roaring Chenab River — inside Seismic Zone Five.
scenes.captionMarkup: Between *Bakkal* and *Kauri* lies a sheer canyon above the *Chenab River* — inside *Seismic Zone V.*

scenes.voiceoverText: India spanned it at 359 metres above the riverbed! That is 35 metres taller than the Eiffel Tower in Paris!
scenes.captionMarkup: India spanned it at *359 metres* above the river — *35 metres taller* than the *Eiffel Tower!*

scenes.voiceoverText: Engineers lifted 28,660 tonnes of steel across a 467-metre arch — using giant overhead cable cranes suspended in thin air!
scenes.captionMarkup: Engineers lifted *28,660 tonnes* of steel across a *467-metre arch* using *giant cable cranes!*

scenes.voiceoverText: With DRDO, they armoured it in 63-millimetre blast-proof steel, concrete-filled piers, and sensors that keep trains safe even if one pier fails.
scenes.captionMarkup: With *DRDO,* they used *63mm blast-proof steel,* concrete piers, and *real-time structural sensors.*

scenes.voiceoverText: Here is that locked number: the bridge withstands 266 kilometre-per-hour cyclonic winds, Magnitude 8 earthquakes, and minus 20 degrees!
scenes.captionMarkup: Unlocked: it withstands *266 km/h winds,* *Magnitude 8.0* quakes, and *-20°C* for *120 years!*

scenes.voiceoverText: And it unlocks the entire 272-kilometre rail link — racing from Jammu and Udhampur, across Chenab and Anji Khad, straight into Srinagar!
scenes.captionMarkup: Unlocking the *272 km* link: *Jammu* to *Udhampur,* *Chenab,* *Anji Khad,* and straight into *Srinagar!*

scenes.voiceoverText: Now, the honest part. Carving 38 tunnels through shifting Himalayan rock took over twenty years and ₹37,000 crore.
scenes.captionMarkup: Now, the *honest* part: carving *38 tunnels* through shifting rock took *20+ years* and *₹37,000 crore.*

scenes.voiceoverText: Today, Vande Bharat glides into Kashmir in three hours, all year round. A normal bridge connects two riverbanks. A 359-metre Himalayan arch unites a nation.
scenes.beatACaption: Today, *Vande Bharat* glides into *Kashmir* in *3 hours* — every single day of the year.
scenes.beatBCaption: A normal bridge connects two *riverbanks.* A *359m Himalayan arch* unites a *nation.*

scenes.voiceoverText: Which marvel amazes you most — Chenab Bridge, Atal Tunnel, or Pamban Bridge? One word below.
